chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Chicago schooling, becoming interested in music, and his mother's death
summary: He went to Phillips high school in Chicago, was not at first interested in music, and his mother died in 1918.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I'm just begining to know you a little bit. I know you're from Chicago -- did you grow up in Chicago?
Well, I spent a certain number of years in Chicago. Not too many, I lived mainly in New York.
You were in New York City when?
Early in life.
You went to school in New York City, then?
Oh, no, no. I went to school in Chicago.
You graduated from high school?
Yes.
What school did you graduate from?
Phillips.
How did you first get started in music?
I wasn't interested in music at first.
You were or you were not?
I was not.
No?
I wasn't. No. It didn't bother me, music was just music, something I heard with the rest of people, that was all.
Until what age?
Well, see, I can't remember exact ages, you know? When you get down to pinpointing ages and things, it's a little bit too much.
But you were interested in music in high school?
I loved the music. Sure, I'd listen to it just like any other cat would out there. And we enjoyed it. But being part of it wasn't ...
Not yet. Did people in your family have an interest in it?
No. I was the only kid.
Oh, really?
Yeah, I was the only one.
Turned out a good one.
They turned out one good great one, and they said that was enough!
Well ... my mother was around then. Passed away in 1918. Does that matter? Throw me one
So what did you do? You graduated from high school, and you werent really into music yet ... so what did you do then?
Well, I just jilted around from one place to another. And until I found my way. Just like every other youngster. You got to keep going until you find what you want, and then you stick with it.
Well, you did.
